He was forced to give way to Collins of Shaftesbury who went from 6th to 2nd and Lewis of Woodford (10th to 4th), but was able to displace Blackheath.

Charlie Dabbs ran well on Stage 1 to finish 4th, 18 seconds down on the leader (Collins of Surrey AC), but on the next leg Hyman beat Geoff North in the run-in and, for a moment, both Portsmouth teams were ahead of us.

Belgrave looked set for second after good runs by Laurie O'Hara and Mel Thorpe, but Bob Holt(Herc) squeezed in front of Tony Fairclough on the penultimate leg and Chris Steer was passed by Collins (Windsor) on the last.
I wonder how necessary it was for Dunphy and Murray (Hercules), Kortenray(Wimbledon) Smallbone (Epsom and Ewell) and--almost--Collins (Surrey) to change their's.

The race was now developing into one of the best of the series, Major was determined to keep the Bels within striking distance by moving us up to 3rd. Collins held on to the lead for Hercules/W'don and young Cass ran a good 4¾ miles for Portsmouth.

John Stow, recovering from tonsilitis, hardly treated stage six like a convalescent's outing for he took us up two places overtaking Bartlett of Birchfield and Collins of Hercules Wimbledon in the process.
